pharm: Endogenous steroid hormone; progesterone receptor agonist
tags: Used in HRT and luteal support
quick: HRT (with estrogen): 200 mg oral micronized at bedtime x12-14 days/cycle, or 100 mg daily continuous
Take at bedtime; food increases absorption of oral micronized form
Used in luteal support / threatened miscarriage; otherwise per indication
Small amounts in milk; generally considered compatible
Endometrial protection, BP, mood, breast exam, VTE signs
summary: Progesterone is the natural progestogen used for endometrial protection during estrogen hormone therapy, secondary amenorrhea, and luteal-phase/early-pregnancy support (vaginal route). Oral micronized progesterone is sedating and is taken at bedtime. It opposes estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation.
indications: Prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in postmenopausal women receiving estrogen (women with a uterus)
Luteal phase support in assisted reproduction (vaginal)
Support of early pregnancy / threatened or recurrent miscarriage (vaginal, region/guideline dependent)
Dysfunctional uterine bleeding due to progesterone deficiency

dosage.d: 200 mg once daily at bedtime for 12-14 days per 28-day cycle, OR 100 mg daily continuous combined
dosage.n: Always combine with estrogen in women with uterus

dosage.d: 400 mg once daily at bedtime for 10 days
90 mg gel once daily (or 100-200 mg vaginal capsule 2-3 times daily per protocol)
dosage.n: Continue per IVF protocol, often into early pregnancy

dosage.d: 400 mg twice daily until ~16 weeks gestation

admin: Oral micronized: take at bedtime, ideally on an empty stomach for consistent absorption; expect drowsiness/dizziness
Do not drive or operate machinery shortly after an oral dose
Vaginal route: insert as directed; preferred for luteal/pregnancy support (first-pass uterine delivery)
Confirm presence of intact uterus and concomitant estrogen for HRT indication
Note peanut allergy: some micronized capsules contain peanut oil
moa: Binds progesterone receptors to transform an estrogen-primed proliferative endometrium into a secretory endometrium, opposing estrogen-induced proliferation and reducing hyperplasia/carcinoma risk. It supports implantation and maintenance of early pregnancy and produces negative feedback on gonadotropin secretion.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (or to peanut for peanut-oil capsules)
Active or history of arterial/venous thromboembolism (DVT, PE, stroke, MI)

preg: Used therapeutically for luteal support and threatened/recurrent miscarriage (vaginal route) under specialist guidance; bioidentical progesterone is not associated with fetal harm at these doses. Not indicated for routine non-supportive use in pregnancy.
lact: Detectable in small amounts in breast milk; progesterone-only progestogens are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding. Monitor the infant; use if clearly needed.
renal: Limited specific data; use with caution in significant renal impairment and monitor for fluid retention.
hepatic: Contraindicated in liver dysfunction or disease; hepatically metabolized. Avoid in active hepatic disorders and monitor liver function if risk factors present.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) reduce progesterone efficacy
Estrogens (used together intentionally in HRT - combined VTE considerations)
moderate: CNS depressants (additive sedation with oral form)
interactions.food: Food increases bioavailability of oral micronized progesterone; standardize timing relative to meals
interactions.alcohol: Avoid with oral form due to enhanced drowsiness and dizziness
interactions.diagnostics: May affect coagulation, thyroid, and liver function test parameters

emergency: Signs of clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness, sudden severe headache, visual loss

monitoring: Endometrial response and abnormal bleeding (investigate persistent/recurrent bleeding)
Liver function if hepatic risk factors
counsel: Take the oral capsule at bedtime; it may make you sleepy - avoid driving afterward
Avoid alcohol with the oral form
Report unusual vaginal bleeding, leg or chest pain, breathlessness, or sudden severe headache
Tell your clinician about peanut allergy before using oil-based capsules
Perform regular breast self-checks and attend screening
Do not stop estrogen+progesterone HRT abruptly without advice
pk: Oral: within hours; sedation soon after dosing
20-25°C (68-77°F); protect from light; do not freeze gel/capsules
pearls: Always pair with estrogen for endometrial protection in women with a uterus on estrogen HRT
Vaginal route gives high local uterine concentration with less systemic sedation - preferred for fertility/pregnancy support
Oral micronized progesterone is bioidentical and may have a more favorable metabolic/VTE profile than synthetic progestins
Bedtime dosing leverages the sedative effect and minimizes daytime drowsiness
Check capsule excipients for peanut oil in allergic patients
missed: Take a missed oral dose as soon as remembered the same evening; if it is nearly the next day's dose, skip it and resume the bedtime schedule. For vaginal/luteal support, follow the specific protocol and contact the clinic if a dose is missed.
overdose: Overdose chiefly causes drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, and breast tenderness. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive and symptomatic care and dose reduction. Severe somnolence may occur with high oral doses.
